00244.label: Regorafenib oral cycle: Days 1–21, then Days 22–28 off

medicines.name: Rescue antiemetic
medicines.dose: Individual prescription under the oral-SACT pathway
medicines.timing: As required, not routine daily prophylaxis
medicines.note: NCCP V6 Table 5 offers metoclopramide, prochlorperazine or one 5-HT3 antagonist. Choose and prescribe one appropriate option after contraindication, interaction, renal-function and QT review; do not combine alternatives automatically.

additional_support: No routine premedication is usually required. Provide local hand–foot skin reaction prevention and treatment; examine pressure areas and report pain, blisters or impaired walking early.
Take the prescribed dose once daily after a light meal containing less than 30% fat, as clarified by current Stivarga SmPC; do not replace a vomited dose or double the next day.
Check liver tests every two weeks for the first two months, then monthly or as clinically indicated; abnormalities require the separate source-specific closer monitoring plan.

Check blood pressure weekly for the first six weeks, then before each cycle or as clinically indicated. Baseline thyroid testing; subsequent thyroid, lipase and amylase checks as clinically indicated.
Review strong CYP3A4/UGT interactions, bleeding, infection, ischaemia, wounds and planned surgery; close INR monitoring if taking warfarin.
Dose changes require consultant review. HFSR recovery, occurrence count and previous dose determine the pathway; permitted re-escalation is not a patient-led action.

guidance.label: NCCP 00244 v5 and NCCP oral antiemetic guidance V6 Table 5, p8

00382.label: Cyclic oral monotherapy: moderate-to-high emetic risk

medicines.name: One oral 5-HT3 antagonist (choose one)
medicines.dose: NCCP oral reference options: granisetron 1–2 mg total daily OR ondansetron 8–16 mg total daily
medicines.timing: Start before oral treatment and continue daily according to the prescribed course; team specifies dosing and rest-day coverage
medicines.note: Alternatives, not concurrent prescriptions. Assess QT risk, constipation, interacting medicines, organ function and local formulary. No routine added steroid is inferred from parenteral guidance.

additional_support: Agree oral preventive antiemetic and rescue instructions under NCCP oral guidance/local policy; this is not the NCIS parenteral moderate/high protocol.
No routine premedication is specified by NCCP 00382.
Assess need for G-CSF or other infection support individually; no universal prophylaxis is prescribed here.
Use the exact dosing calendar and no catch-up doses.
Reconcile GI symptoms, hydration and additional blood counts for renal impairment.

Confirm the body-surface-area prescription, actual morning and evening tablet counts and Days 1–5 and 8–12 calendar. Take within one hour after breakfast and the evening meal; do not replace missed or vomited doses.

Follow current NCCP cycle-start blood and urine checks and the additional EMA blood-count requirement before starting and as needed, at minimum before each cycle; increase monitoring with renal impairment or toxicity.
Prior reductions must be retained: no dose re-escalation. The severe-renal dosing pathway differs from the standard minimum dose and needs separate review.

guidance.label: NCCP oral SACT antiemetic guidance V6, section 4.2 and Table 5; NCIS V8 is parenteral context

00207.label: First cetuximab dose

medicines.name: Chlorphenamine
medicines.timing: 60 minutes before cetuximab
medicines.note: NCCP suggested premedication.

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.timing: 60 minutes before cetuximab
medicines.note: NCCP suggested mandatory infusion premedication; reconcile low-risk antiemetic support to avoid duplicate steroid.

medicines.name: Rescue antiemetic
medicines.timing: If required
medicines.note: Low emetic risk; use current NCCP/local guidance and account for the infusion steroid.

additional_support: Skin care and sun protection under local EGFR policy.
First two doses require post-infusion observation; delayed-reaction education.
Monthly electrolytes/Mg/Ca for two months after last dose.

guidance.label: NCCP NCIS Medical Oncology antiemetics V8, Table 1

00207.label: Subsequent weekly cetuximab

medicines.name: Chlorphenamine
medicines.timing: 60 minutes before each infusion

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.timing: 60 minutes before each infusion
medicines.note: Reconcile antiemetic steroid; no automatic duplication.

additional_support: Premedication continues for subsequent infusions.
Head/neck RT requires separate mucosal, skin, swallow and nutrition support.
Post-treatment monthly electrolytes/Mg/Ca for two months.

guidance.label: NCCP NCIS Medical Oncology antiemetics V8, Table 1

00225.label: Day 1 · antibody monotherapy

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.timing: Before panitumumab, according to the individual antiemetic prescription
medicines.note: NCIS V8 low-risk row. Routine infusion-reaction premedication is a separate issue and is not usually required for panitumumab.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg PO up to three times daily as required
medicines.timing: Rescue nausea treatment only as prescribed
medicines.note: NCIS V8 rescue option; check contraindications, renal function, interactions and prescribed duration.

additional_support: Antiemetic classification refers to the active treatment day. Reconcile duplicate steroid entries before prescribing.
No automatic G-CSF schedule is added; use the patient’s neutropenia history, risk and consultant plan.
No routine cetuximab-style antihistamine/steroid premedication is imported into panitumumab.
Provide local EGFR skin care, periodic magnesium/calcium/potassium checks and monthly post-treatment electrolytes for two months.

guidance.label: NCCP NCIS antiemetics V8 (2025), Table 1 and multi-day principles

00328.label: Day 1 · chemotherapy and antibody

medicines.name: Antihistamine
medicines.dose: As prescribed in the local cetuximab premedication plan
medicines.timing: At least one hour before cetuximab
medicines.note: Repeat for subsequent cetuximab infusions; assess prior infusion reactions.

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.dose: 8 mg PO once, subject to reconciliation with the cetuximab premedication prescription
medicines.timing: At least one hour before cetuximab on Day 1
medicines.note: This corticosteroid also covers the treatment-day corticosteroid part of antiemesis where appropriate. Pharmacy must reconcile route, dose and timing; do not automatically add a second 8 mg antiemetic dose.

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.timing: Before Day 1 chemotherapy
medicines.note: NCIS V8 moderate-risk row; consider QT risk, low electrolytes, interactions and the individual prescription.

medicines.name: Dexamethasone
medicines.timing: Days 2 and 3 after the administered Day 1 chemotherapy
medicines.note: NCIS V8 delayed prophylaxis. Reconcile with any other steroid prescription; re-anchor dates if treatment is delayed.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg PO up to three times daily as required
medicines.timing: Rescue nausea treatment only as prescribed
medicines.note: NCIS V8 rescue option; check contraindications, renal function, interactions and prescribed duration.

medicines.name: Atropine sulphate
medicines.timing: Before irinotecan when prescribed; assess acute cholinergic symptoms
medicines.note: Avoid in glaucoma. This treats/prevents the acute cholinergic syndrome; it is not the delayed-diarrhoea rescue medicine.

additional_support: Antiemetic classification refers to the active treatment day. Reconcile duplicate steroid entries before prescribing.
No automatic G-CSF schedule is added; use the patient’s neutropenia history, risk and consultant plan.
Cetuximab premedication and infusion observation remain necessary even on an antibody-only day.
Start local EGFR skin care; monitor magnesium, calcium and potassium before and periodically during therapy, then monthly for two months after the final dose.

Provide a written irinotecan delayed-diarrhoea rescue and escalation plan before treatment; distinguish it from immediate infusion-related cramps/sweating. Fever, severe pain, dehydration or diarrhoea not responding to the prescribed plan needs urgent review.
Confirm line care, pump contact details and disconnection arrangements; report chest pain, severe early fluorouracil toxicity or pump/line problems urgently.

Supply a written irinotecan delayed-diarrhoea rescue prescription: NCCP reference loperamide 4 mg initially, then 2 mg every 2 hours; continue for 12 hours after the last liquid stool, never longer than 48 hours at this high-dose schedule. Start electrolyte-containing fluids. Fever, dehydration, severe pain or persistent symptoms require urgent oncology review. This is distinct from acute cholinergic symptoms treated with atropine.

guidance.label: NCCP NCIS antiemetics V8 (2025), Table 1 and multi-day principles

00328.label: Day 8 · weekly cetuximab only

medicines.name: Antihistamine
medicines.timing: At least one hour before cetuximab
medicines.note: Cetuximab premedication remains applicable.

medicines.name: Corticosteroid
medicines.timing: At least one hour before cetuximab
medicines.note: Reconcile low-risk antiemesis with this corticosteroid; do not duplicate steroids.

medicines.name: Metoclopramide
medicines.dose: 10 mg PO up to three times daily as required
medicines.timing: Rescue only as prescribed
medicines.note: No automatic delayed steroid course is carried over from Day 1 chemotherapy.

additional_support: Cetuximab only: no irinotecan, oxaliplatin, fluorouracil or atropine is scheduled on Day 8.
Continue skin care, electrolyte monitoring, infusion precautions and the urgent contact plan.
Low-risk antibody-only antiemesis is distinct from Day 1 moderate-risk chemotherapy prophylaxis.

guidance.label: NCCP NCIS antiemetics V8 low-risk row
